arguments.name: project
arguments.description: Project path or name (defaults to the current directory)

options.description: Build target (e.g. StandaloneWindows64, Android, iOS, WebGL). Required unless --profile is used.
Static C# method to invoke (e.g. Builder.PerformBuild). Optional: without it, the CLI uses Unity's built-in build — a build profile on Unity 6+, or the legacy desktop player flags.
Build profile to build with: a path to a .asset file, or a profile name in Assets/Settings/Build Profiles (Unity 6+ only; the profile defines the target)
Optional build target group, forwarded to Unity as -buildTargetGroup
Output path for the build. Forwarded as -buildOutput with --execute-method (your method is responsible for honoring it); otherwise the built-in build's destination, and required
Log file path (default: <project>/Logs/build-<target>-<timestamp>.log). The log also streams to the console by default; --no-tail disables it.
Override editor version (default: from ProjectVersion.txt)
Path to a specific editor binary
Editor architecture (x86_64 or arm64) (default: "unknown")
Extra arguments passed to Unity (shell-split)
Do not stream the log to stdout in real time
Install the project's editor version if it is not already installed
Android export type: apk, aab, or android-studio-project (Android targets only, default: apk) (choices: "apk", "aab", "android-studio-project", default: "apk")
Base64-encoded keystore file contents — decoded to a temp file before the build and deleted after (Android targets only; warning: CLI args may appear in shell history and CI logs)
Password for the keystore (Android targets only, required with --android-keystore-base64; warning: CLI args may appear in shell history and CI logs)
Key alias inside the keystore (Android targets only, required with --android-keystore-base64)
Password for the key alias (Android targets only, defaults to --android-keystore-password; warning: CLI args may appear in shell history and CI logs)
Android SDK target version integer, e.g. 34 (Android targets only)
Debug symbol export type: none, public, or debugging (Android targets only, default: none) (choices: "none", "public", "debugging", default: "none")
Explicit Android versionCode integer (Android targets only)
Versioning strategy to apply to the build (semantic, tag, custom, none). Default: none. (choices: "semantic", "tag", "custom", "none", default: "none")
Explicit version string to stamp on the build. Only used when --versioning-strategy is 'custom'; ignored for all other strategies.
Skip the uncommitted-changes guard (default: false) (default: false)
Abort the build if it runs longer than this many seconds (disabled by default) (env: UNITY_BUILD_TIMEOUT)
Where to write the build provenance manifest (default: beside the build output, or beside the log file when --output-path is not set)
Do not write the build provenance manifest

extra_sections.heading: Notes
lines: --vcs-namespace and --vcs-repo apply to BOTH providers (there is no --git-namespace/--git-repo here).
--ref: an all-digits UVCS ref is read as a changeset, otherwise as a branch.
Git LFS assets are fetched automatically (needs git-lfs installed). Use --no-lfs to leave pointer files.
Git tokens are owned by your Git credential manager, not the CLI, which stores nothing you pass or enter.
For a different token per organization, set credential.useHttpPath true, or install Git Credential Manager.
In multi-org CI, pass --git-token per invocation: UNITY_GITHUB_TOKEN / UNITY_GITLAB_TOKEN hold one token per provider.
Self-hosted or enterprise host: each host signs in separately. Sign in with its own CLI
(gh auth login --hostname <host>, glab auth login --hostname <host>,
tea login add --name <name> --url https://<host>), or let Git Credential Manager store one
credential per host. An SSH URL needs neither, using your SSH agent instead.

subcommands.name: setup
subcommands.summary: Get this project into version control and push a first commit, asking only what cannot be detected

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.summary: Show what changed, grouped by what it means to Unity, with meta-file pairing problems

subcommands.name: sync
subcommands.summary: Pull safely: refuse while an Editor holds the project, pull the commits and the LFS objects, then report the reimport

subcommands.name: doctor
subcommands.summary: Check the repository settings, ignore rules, LFS patterns, and package pinning a Unity project needs under version control

subcommands.name: providers
subcommands.summary: Report which git provider this machine can reach, as whom, and what each host allows

subcommands.name: merge-setup
subcommands.summary: Make Unity scene and prefab merges work in this repository, using the editor's UnityYAMLMerge tool

subcommands.name: switch
subcommands.summary: Switch branches safely: refuse while an Editor holds the project, then report the reimport the switch causes

subcommands.name: conflicts
subcommands.summary: List unresolved merge conflicts, classified by Unity type, with whether each one can merge automatically

subcommands.name: explain
subcommands.summary: Explain in plain language what each branch changed in a conflicted Unity asset

subcommands.name: resolve
subcommands.summary: Resolve a conflicted Unity asset with UnityYAMLMerge, or by taking one side

subcommands.name: diff
subcommands.summary: Diff a scene or prefab by object and component name instead of by file id

subcommands.name: summarize
subcommands.summary: Summarize what a branch changed, ready to paste into a pull request

subcommands.name: affected
subcommands.summary: Report which assets, assemblies, and tests a change affects

subcommands.name: hooks
subcommands.summary: Manage the git hooks that run the Unity integrity checks at commit time

subcommands.name: git
subcommands.summary: Git-only verbs, for the things UVCS has no equivalent of

subcommands.name: uvcs
subcommands.summary: Unity Version Control reads that join cm's data to your project

subcommands.name: help
subcommands.summary: display help for command

examples: unity vcs setup                 Set this project up for version control
unity vcs setup --vcs github    Skip the provider question and use GitHub
unity vcs status                Group your changes the way Unity sees them
unity vcs sync                  Pull safely, with the LFS objects
unity vcs doctor                Audit this repository's Unity source-control setup
unity vcs doctor --fix          Audit it and repair everything repairable
unity vcs providers             Report which git provider is ready here
unity vcs merge-setup           Make scene and prefab merges work here
unity vcs merge-setup --check   Report what needs setting up, change nothing
unity vcs switch main           Switch to the main branch
unity vcs switch main --dry-run Report what the switch costs, change nothing
unity vcs conflicts             List conflicts by Unity type
unity vcs explain <path>        Explain what each branch changed
unity vcs resolve --all         Merge every auto-resolvable conflict
unity vcs diff <path>           Read a scene change by object name
unity vcs summarize --since dev Summarize the branch for a pull request
unity vcs affected --since main Report what a branch's changes affect
unity vcs hooks install         Install the Unity git hooks
unity vcs hooks status          See which hooks are installed
unity vcs git migrate-lfs       Cost the binaries already in git history
unity vcs git worktree add x    Work on a second branch without a cold reimport
unity vcs uvcs locks            See who holds a Unity Version Control lock
